s0101.literal: He struck straight at Hefei and entered its outer wall.
s0101.idiomatic: He struck straight at Hefei and entered its outer suburbs.

s0103.literal: For merit he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfu County with a fief of five hundred households.
s0103.idiomatic: For merit he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and enfeoffed as marquis of Anfu county with a fief of five hundred households.

s0104.literal: When the armies were destroyed at Lüliang, Zhong brought his army back intact.
s0104.idiomatic: When the armies were destroyed at Lüliang, Zhong brought his army back intact.

s0105.literal: Soon an edict made Zhong area commander over the armies along the Huai at Shouyang, Xincai, and Huo; he was promoted to Ningyuan General and Inspector of Huo.
s0105.idiomatic: Soon an edict made Zhong commander of the armies along the Huai at Shouyang, Xincai, and Huo; he was promoted to ningyuan general and inspector of Huo.

s0106.literal: He entered court as Left Guard General.
s0106.idiomatic: He entered court as left guard general.

s0107.literal: In the eleventh year he was additionally made commander of the northern expedition vanguard, promoted to Pacify-North General, and led infantry and cavalry toward Qin Commandery.
s0107.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was additionally made commander of the northern expedition vanguard, promoted to pacify-north general, and led infantry and cavalry toward Qin commandery.

s0108.literal: In the twelfth year he was moved to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Area Commander over Southern Yuzhou military affairs, Pacify-South General, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; his fief was increased with the former to one thousand five hundred households.
s0108.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made bearer of the staff, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, commander over Southern Yuzhou military affairs, pacify-south general, and inspector of Southern Yuzhou; his fief was increased with the former to one thousand five hundred households.

s0109.literal: He still led infantry and cavalry toward Liyang.
s0109.idiomatic: He still led infantry and cavalry toward Liyang.

s0110.literal: Northern Zhou sent Wang Yanging leading troops as relief; Zhong inflicted a great defeat and captured Yanging alive.
s0110.idiomatic: Northern Zhou sent Wang Yanging with troops in relief; Zhong routed them and captured Yanging alive.

s0111.literal: When the Later Lord succeeded, Zhong was promoted to Garrison-South General and given one set of pipes and drums.
s0111.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded, Zhong was promoted to garrison-south general and given one set of pipes and drums.

s0112.literal: He entered court as Commander of the Army, was additionally made Palace Attendant, and was re-enfeoffed as Liangxin
s0112.idiomatic: He entered court as commander of the army, was also made palace attendant, and was re-enfeoffed as Liangxin

s0114.literal: Commandery Duke, Editorial footnote marker 8. fief three thousand households.
s0114.idiomatic: commandery duke [8] with a fief of three thousand households.

s0115.literal: He went out as Interior Minister of Wuxing with rank at two thousand shi of grain.
s0115.idiomatic: He went out as interior minister of Wuxing with rank at two thousand shi of grain.

s0116.literal: When Sui forces crossed the Yangtze, Zhong came in from Wuxing and garrisoned at the Vermilion Bird Gate.
s0116.idiomatic: When Sui forces crossed the Yangtze, Zhong came in from Wuxing and garrisoned at the Vermilion Bird Gate.

s0117.literal: The Later Lord summoned Xiao Mohe and others to the inner hall for deliberation; Zhong pressed his view, saying: "Military writers say guest and host differ in strength—the guest values swift battle, the host values weight.
s0117.idiomatic: Houzhu summoned Xiao Mohe and others to the inner hall for deliberation. Zhong pressed his view: "Writers on war say guest and host differ in strength—the guest should fight swiftly, the host should hold firm.

s0118.literal: For now we should add troops and hold the palace city fast, send the fleet in detachments toward Southern Yuzhou and the Jingkou route, and cut the invaders' grain transport.
s0118.idiomatic: We should add troops and hold the palace city, send the fleet in detachments toward Southern Yuzhou and the Jingkou route, and cut the enemy's grain transport.

s0119.literal: When spring waters rise, the upstream armies under Zhou Luohou and others will surely come downriver in relief—this is the sound plan."
s0119.idiomatic: When spring waters rise, the upstream armies under Zhou Luohou and others will surely come downriver in relief. That is the sound plan."

s0120.literal: The assembly disagreed, and so they went out to battle.
s0120.idiomatic: The assembly disagreed, and they went out to battle.

s0121.literal: When defeated, Zhong galloped into the palace to see the Later Lord, reported the defeat, and memorialized: "Your Majesty need only ready boats and go to the upstream armies; your servant will guard you unto death."
s0121.idiomatic: When defeated, Zhong galloped into the palace, reported the defeat, and said, "Your Majesty need only ready boats and go to the upstream armies; I will guard you unto death."

s0122.literal: The Later Lord believed him and ordered Zhong to go out and make dispositions; Zhong declined, saying: "When your servant has finished the arrangements, I shall come to escort you."
s0122.idiomatic: Houzhu believed him and ordered Zhong to go out and make dispositions. Zhong declined: "When I have finished the arrangements, I shall come to escort you."

s0123.literal: The Later Lord had palace women dress and wait for Zhong, but long watched in vain for his coming.
s0123.idiomatic: Houzhu had palace women dress and wait for Zhong, but watched in vain for a long time.

s0124.literal: Sui General Han Qinhu advanced from Xinlin; Zhong then led several horsemen to Shizi Mound to surrender to him, and led Qinhu's army together through the South Side Gate.
s0124.idiomatic: Sui general Han Qinhu advanced from Xinlin; Zhong then led several horsemen to Shizi Mound to surrender, and led Qinhu's army in together through the South Side Gate.

s0125.literal: When the capital fell, that year he entered Chang'an; Sui appointed him Honored Companion with Protocol Equal to the Three Lords.
s0125.idiomatic: When the capital fell, that year he entered Chang'an; Sui made him honored companion with protocol equal to the three lords.

s0127.literal: His son Youwu rose to Honored Companion with Protocol Equal to the Three Lords.
s0127.idiomatic: His son Youwu rose to honored companion with protocol equal to the three lords.

s0128.literal: At the time there was Shen Keqing, a man of Wukang in Wuxing; by nature crafty, fawning, and cruel, he served as Secretariat Attendant; he always set up odd schemes and made cutting down the common people his sole business, and thereby advanced himself.
s0128.idiomatic: At the time there was Shen Keqing of Wukang in Wuxing—crafty, fawning, and cruel. As secretariat attendant he always devised odd schemes and made squeezing the people his sole business, and thereby advanced himself.

s0129.literal: There was also Shi Wenqing, a man of Wucheng in Wuxing; rising from the lowest ranks, he had skill in clerical work; the Later Lord pulled him up as chief secretary, moved him to Secretariat Attendant, and soon promoted him to Inspector of Xiangzhou.
s0129.idiomatic: There was also Shi Wenqing of Wucheng in Wuxing, who rose from the lowest ranks with skill in clerical work. Houzhu pulled him up as chief secretary, made him secretariat attendant, and soon promoted him to inspector of Xiangzhou.

s0130.literal: Before he could take up the post, Sui forces came to attack; prefectures and garrisons everywhere reported in succession.
s0130.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Sui forces came to attack; prefectures and garrisons everywhere reported in succession.

s0131.literal: Wenqing and Keqing both held confidential power; all outside memorials and reports passed through them for presentation.
s0131.idiomatic: Wenqing and Keqing both held confidential power; all outside memorials and reports passed through them for presentation.

s0132.literal: Wenqing was pleased by the weight of Xiangzhou and wished to go early; he and Keqing worked inside and outside together, suppressing reports and saying nothing, and the Later Lord did not know—thus through lack of preparation the state was lost; truly the crime of these two men.
s0132.idiomatic: Wenqing coveted the weight of Xiangzhou and wished to go early; he and Keqing worked in concert, suppressing reports, and Houzhu knew nothing—through lack of preparation the state was lost; truly these two were to blame.

s0133.literal: When Sui forces had entered, both were executed before the front gate.
s0133.idiomatic: When Sui forces entered, both were executed before the front gate.

s0134.literal: Fan Yi, styled Zhilie, was a man of Huyang in Nanyang.
s0134.idiomatic: Fan Yi, styled Zhilie, was from Huyang in Nanyang.

s0135.literal: His grandfather Fangxing was Liang's Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Benevolent Might General, Inspector of Sizhou, and Marquis of Yufu County.
s0135.idiomatic: His grandfather Fangxing was Liang's regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, benevolent might general, inspector of Sizhou, and marquis of Yufu county.

s0136.literal: His father Wenci was Liang's Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Trustworthy Martial General, Inspector of Yizhou, and Marquis of Xincai County.
s0136.idiomatic: His father Wenci was Liang's regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, trustworthy martial general, inspector of Yizhou, and marquis of Xincai county.

s0137.literal: Yi came from many generations of a general house; in youth he practiced arms and was skilled at archery.
s0137.idiomatic: Yi came from many generations of a general house; in youth he practiced arms and was skilled at archery.

s0138.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Yi led his private troops following his uncle Wenjiao to relieve the capital.
s0138.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Yi led his private troops following his uncle Wenjiao to relieve the capital.

s0139.literal: Wenjiao died in battle at Qingxi; Yi led clan youths to Jiangling and then attached to Wang Sengbian, campaigning against the Prince of Hedong Xiao Yu; for merit he was made Acting Commander, Might-of-Armies General, and Right Central Commandant.
s0139.idiomatic: Wenjiao died in battle at Qingxi; Yi led clan youths to Jiangling and attached to Wang Sengbian in the campaign against the Prince of Hedong Xiao Yu. For merit he was made acting commander, might-of-armies general, and right central commandant.

s0140.literal: He replaced his elder brother Jun as Administrator of Liangxing, commanded roaming troops of three provinces, and followed the Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun to campaign against Lu Na in Xiangzhou.
s0140.idiomatic: He replaced his elder brother Jun as administrator of Liangxing, commanded roaming troops of three provinces, and followed the Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun against Lu Na in Xiangzhou.

s0141.literal: When the army halted at Baling the camp was not yet set; Na sent troops by night, pressed the camp with great clamor, and officers and men in camp were all alarmed; Yi alone with several dozen men on his left and right held the camp gate and fought hard, beheading more than ten heads, beat the drum to proclaim orders, and the host was then settled.
s0141.idiomatic: When the army halted at Baling the camp was not yet set. Na sent troops by night, pressed the camp with a great clamor, and the men were alarmed. Yi alone with several dozen men held the camp gate and fought hard, beheading more than ten, beat the drum to proclaim orders, and the host was then settled.

s0142.literal: For merit he was made Bearer of the Staff, Direct and Upright Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Upright Might General, enfeoffed as Baron of Yidao County with a fief of three hundred households.
s0142.idiomatic: For merit he was made bearer of the staff, direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, and upright might general, enfeoffed as baron of Yidao county with a fief of three hundred households.

s0143.literal: Soon he was made Administrator of Tianmen, advanced in rank to Marquis, and his fief was increased with the former to one thousand households.
s0143.idiomatic: Soon he was made administrator of Tianmen, advanced to marquis, and his fief was increased with the former to one thousand households.

s0144.literal: When Western Wei besieged Jiangling, Yi led troops to relieve it; Jiangling fell and he was seized by the Prince of Yueyang; after a long while he escaped and returned.
s0144.idiomatic: When Western Wei besieged Jiangling, Yi led troops to relieve it. Jiangling fell and he was seized by the Prince of Yueyang; after a long while he escaped and returned.

s0145.literal: When the High Emperor received the abdication, Yi and his younger brother Meng raised troops in response to Wang Lin; Lin was defeated and fled to Qi; Grand Marshal Hou Tian sent envoys to summon Yi; Yi led sons, nephews, and private troops back to court.
s0145.idiomatic: When the High Emperor received the abdication, Yi and his younger brother Meng raised troops for Wang Lin. Lin was defeated and fled to Qi; grand marshal Hou Tian sent envoys to summon Yi, and Yi led sons, nephews, and private troops back to court.

s0146.literal: In the second year of Tiankang he was made Direct and Upright Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and still followed Hou Tian in the advance against Ba and Xiang.
s0146.idiomatic: In Tiankang year 2 he was made direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry and still followed Hou Tian against Ba and Xiang.

s0147.literal: By successive promotions he became Inspector of Wuzhou.
s0147.idiomatic: By successive promotions he became inspector of Wuzhou.

s0148.literal: At the beginning of Taikian he was moved to Inspector of Fengzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaochang County with a fief of one thousand households.
s0148.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taikian he was moved to inspector of Fengzhou and enfeoffed as marquis of Gaochang county with a fief of one thousand households.

s0149.literal: He entered court as Left Guard General.
s0149.idiomatic: He entered court as left guard general.

s0150.literal: In the fifth year of the great northern expedition Yi led troops to attack Chuzi Fort at Guangling, took it, drove off Qi forces at the mouth of the Ying, Qi relief came to Cangling and was again defeated; in the seventh year he advanced and captured Tongzhou, Xiapi, Gaozha, and six other cities.
s0150.idiomatic: In year 5 of the great northern expedition Yi led troops against Chuzi Fort at Guangling and took it, drove off Qi forces at the mouth of the Ying, and when Qi relief came to Cangling defeated it again. In year 7 he advanced and captured Tongzhou, Xiapi, Gaozha, and six other cities.

s0151.literal: When Lüliang lost its armies, an edict made Yi supreme commander, promoted him to Pacify-North General, led troops across the Huai, built a fort opposite Qingkou to resist the Zhou, rain in torrents ruined the wall, and Yi brought the whole army out intact.
s0151.idiomatic: When Lüliang lost its armies, an edict made Yi supreme commander and promoted him to pacify-north general. He led troops across the Huai, built a fort opposite Qingkou to resist Zhou, torrential rain ruined the wall, and Yi brought the whole army out intact.

s0152.literal: Soon he was moved to Central Army Commander.
s0152.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to central army commander.

s0153.literal: In the eleventh year Zhou General Liang Shiyan led troops to besiege Shouyang; an edict made Yi commander of the northern expedition vanguard, Editorial footnote marker 9. and he led the fleet into Jiao Lake.
s0153.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Zhou general Liang Shiyan led troops to besiege Shouyang; an edict made Yi commander of the northern expedition vanguard [9], and he led the fleet into Jiao Lake.

s0154.literal: Soon he was made Garrison-West General and Area Commander over the land and water forces of the four provinces Jing, Ying, Ba, and Wu.
s0154.idiomatic: Soon he was made garrison-west general and commander over the land and water forces of Jing, Ying, Ba, and Wu.

s0155.literal: In the twelfth year he was advanced to command the armies of Mian and Han; he was dismissed for a public matter.
s0155.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was advanced to command the armies of Mian and Han and was dismissed for a public matter.

s0156.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned and made Central Protector of the Army.
s0156.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was summoned and made central protector of the army.

s0157.literal: Soon he was moved to Protector General and Inspector of Jingzhou.
s0157.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to protector general and inspector of Jingzhou.

s0158.literal: When the Later Lord took the throne, Yi was promoted to Campaign-West General, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xiaoyao Commandery with a fief of three thousand households, the rest as before.
s0158.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne, Yi was promoted to campaign-west general, re-enfeoffed as duke of Xiaoyao commandery with a fief of three thousand households, other offices unchanged.

s0159.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant and Protector General.
s0159.idiomatic: He entered court as palace attendant and protector general.

s0160.literal: When Sui forces crossed the Yangtze, Yi said to Secretariat Director Yuan Xian: "Jingkou and Caishi are both vital points; each needs several thousand elite troops and two hundred golden-wing [ships] to patrol the river above and below the capital for defense.
s0160.idiomatic: When Sui forces crossed the Yangtze, Yi said to secretariat director Yuan Xian, "Jingkou and Caishi are both vital points; each needs several thousand elite troops and two hundred golden-wing ships to patrol the river above and below the capital.

s0161.literal: If not, the great affair is lost."
s0161.idiomatic: If not, the great affair is lost."

s0162.literal: The generals all followed his plan.
s0162.idiomatic: The generals all followed his plan.

s0163.literal: But Shi Wenqing and others suppressed news of Sui troops, and Yi's plan was not carried out.
s0163.idiomatic: But Shi Wenqing and others suppressed news of Sui troops, and Yi's plan was not carried out.

s0164.literal: When the capital fell, he entered the Pass according to precedent; soon he died.
s0164.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he entered the Pass according to precedent; soon he died.

s0165.literal: Meng, styled Zhiwu, was Yi's younger brother.
s0165.idiomatic: Meng, styled Zhiwu, was Yi's younger brother.

s0166.literal: In youth he was bold and unconventional and had capacity and stratagem.
s0166.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and unconventional, with capacity and stratagem.

s0167.literal: When grown he was skilled at bow and horse and his daring surpassed others.
s0167.idiomatic: When grown he was skilled at bow and horse and his daring surpassed others.

s0168.literal: In the battle at Qingxi, from dawn to dusk Meng fought the enemy at close quarters and killed and wounded very many.
s0168.idiomatic: At Qingxi, from dawn to dusk Meng fought the enemy at close quarters and killed and wounded very many.

s0169.literal: When the capital fell he followed his brother Yi west to the western capital; by accumulated battle merit he became Might-of-Armies General.
s0169.idiomatic: When the capital fell he followed his brother Yi west to the western capital and by accumulated battle merit became might-of-armies general.

s0172.literal: Southern [An] Marquis Xiao Fangju was made Inspector of Xiangzhou, Editorial footnote marker 10. and Meng was made Marshal of the Staff.
s0172.idiomatic: Southern [An] marquis Xiao Fangju was made inspector of Xiangzhou [10], and Meng was made marshal of the staff.

s0173.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji raised troops from the Han River eastward, Fangju sent Meng to lead the troops of Xiang and Ying, following Area Commander Lu Fahe in an advance to resist him.
s0173.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji raised troops from the Han River eastward, Fangju sent Meng to lead the troops of Xiang and Ying, following area commander Lu Fahe to resist him.

s0174.literal: At the time Ji had already come downriver; tower ships and war vessels held the Ba River and contested the gorge mouth; they faced each other for a long stalemate and could not decide it.
s0174.idiomatic: Ji had already come downriver; tower ships and war vessels held the Ba River and contested the gorge mouth in a long stalemate that could not be decided.

s0175.literal: Fahe judged Ji's army weary and troops slack; he therefore ordered Meng to lead three thousand elite men in more than a hundred light boats upstream straight up, taking him unawares, with drums and clamor pressing close.
s0175.idiomatic: Fahe judged Ji's army weary and troops slack and ordered Meng to lead three thousand elite men in more than a hundred light boats straight upstream, taking him unawares with drums and clamor pressing close.

s0176.literal: Ji's host in haste was startled and had no time to form ranks; all abandoned their ships and went ashore, and those who drowned numbered in the thousands.
s0176.idiomatic: Ji's host was startled in haste and had no time to form ranks; all abandoned their ships and went ashore, and those who drowned numbered in the thousands.

s0177.literal: At the time several hundred of Ji's closest advisers were still at his side; Meng led more than thirty men of his private troops, shielded and spear in hand, straight up onto Ji's boat, glaring and shouting; Ji's attendants all scattered, lying atop one another and not daring to move.
s0177.idiomatic: Several hundred of Ji's closest advisers were still at his side. Meng led more than thirty private troops, shields up and spears level, straight onto Ji's boat, glaring and shouting; Ji's attendants scattered, lying atop one another and not daring to move.

s0178.literal: Meng with his own hand seized Ji and his father and son, three men, and beheaded them in the boat; he gathered all their ships and equipment.
s0178.idiomatic: Meng seized Ji and his father and son—three men—and beheaded them in the boat, and gathered all their ships and equipment.

s0179.literal: For merit he was made Roaming-Cavalry General and enfeoffed as Baron of Anshan County with a fief of one thousand households.
s0179.idiomatic: For merit he was made roaming-cavalry general and enfeoffed as baron of Anshan county with a fief of one thousand households.

s0180.literal: He still advanced to pacify and settle Liang and Yi; the Shu borderlands were all pacified.
s0180.idiomatic: He still advanced to pacify Liang and Yi; the Shu borderlands were all pacified.

s0181.literal: When the army returned he was moved to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Light-Carriage General, and Inspector of Sizhou; he was advanced in rank to Marquis and his fief was increased with the former to two thousand households.
s0181.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made bearer of the staff, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, light-carriage general, and inspector of Sizhou; he was advanced to marquis and his fief was increased with the former to two thousand households.

s0182.literal: Lu Guangda, styled Bianlan, was the younger brother of Lu Xida, Inspector of Wuzhou.
s0182.idiomatic: Lu Guangda, styled Bianlan, was the younger brother of Lu Xida, inspector of Wuzhou.

s0183.literal: In youth he was generous and high-minded, resolved to establish merit and fame, open-minded and fond of scholars; guests sometimes came from afar.
s0183.idiomatic: In youth he was generous and high-minded, resolved on merit and fame, open-minded and fond of scholars; guests sometimes came from afar.

s0184.literal: At the time commanders south of the Yangtze each led private troops, often numbering in the thousands, but the Lu clan had especially many.
s0184.idiomatic: At the time commanders south of the Yangtze each led private troops, often in the thousands, but the Lu clan had especially many.

s0185.literal: On leaving the purple he was made Right Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Prince Shaoling of Liang, moved to Central Military Aide in the establishment of the Duke of Dangyang, Pacify-the-South.
s0185.idiomatic: On leaving the purple he was made right regular attendant in the kingdom of Prince Shaoling of Liang and moved to central military aide in the establishment of the Duke of Dangyang, pacify-the-south.

s0186.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he and his elder brother Xida gathered troops to hold Xincai.
s0186.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he and his elder brother Xida gathered troops to hold Xincai.

s0187.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang by provisional patent made him Acting Commander, Stalwart Martial General, and Inspector of Jinzhou.
s0187.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang by provisional patent made him acting commander, stalwart martial general, and inspector of Jinzhou.

s0188.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Guangda went out of the border to meet and supply the army with provisions; Sengbian said to Shen Jiong: "Lu of Jinzhou is also a host to the royal army on the eastern route.
s0188.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Guangda went out to meet and supply the army. Sengbian said to Shen Jiong, "Lu of Jinzhou is also a host to the royal army on the eastern route.

s0189.literal: " He then led troops to follow Sengbian.
s0189.idiomatic: " He then led troops to follow Sengbian.

s0190.literal: When Jing was pacified he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; the rest as before.
s0190.idiomatic: When Jing was pacified he was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; other offices unchanged.

s0191.literal: When the High Emperor received the abdication, Guangda was made Campaign-Far General and Administrator of Donghai.
s0191.idiomatic: When the High Emperor received the abdication, Guangda was made campaign-far general and administrator of Donghai.

s0192.literal: Soon he was moved to Administrator of Guiyang; he firmly declined and did not accept, and entered court as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
s0192.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to administrator of Guiyang; he firmly declined and entered court as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

s0193.literal: He was made Acting Commander, Trustworthy Martial General, and Administrator of North Xincai.
s0193.idiomatic: He was made acting commander, trustworthy martial general, and administrator of North Xincai.

s0194.literal: Following Wu Mingche in the campaign against Zhou Di at Linchuan, in every battle his merit ranked first.
s0194.idiomatic: Following Wu Mingche against Zhou Di at Linchuan, in every battle his merit ranked first.

s0195.literal: He still replaced his elder brother Xida as Inspector of Wuzhou, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongsu County with a fief of five hundred households.
s0195.idiomatic: He still replaced his elder brother Xida as inspector of Wuzhou and was enfeoffed as marquis of Zhongsu county with a fief of five hundred households.

s0200.literal: first year, Editorial footnote marker 11. he was made Direct and Upright Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Area Commander over Southern Yuzhou military affairs, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
s0200.idiomatic: First year [11] he was made direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, commander over Southern Yuzhou military affairs, and inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
